Yes. The closest match is FUDLR, which targets fairness problems in LLM-based recommender systems without costly full retraining by treating debiasing as machine unlearning: it identifies bias-inducing samples, then estimates and removes their influence on model parameters, improving fairness while preserving recommendation accuracy [2]. This directly fits “erasing the impact of problematic data points without full model updates” for generative recommendation engines [2].

Related work differs in scope and method. CRAGRU also avoids retraining the whole base model, but focuses on user-specific unlearning in recommender systems and mitigating propagation bias via retrieval-augmented generation rather than general fairness debiasing [1]. If protected attributes are unavailable, H-SAL performs post-hoc concept and attribute erasure from textual profiles, showing debiasing can work without direct sensitive labels, though it is studied for helpfulness prediction rather than generative suggestion engines [5].
